conflicts.point: Whether pre-training compute telemetry and export controls can effectively prevent the proliferation of frontier model capabilities.

positions.stance: Argues that monitoring high-end compute clusters via the Bureau of Industry and Security provides necessary leverage to prevent unaligned frontier training runs.
Argues that once weights are trained, hardware chokepoints become irrelevant because the resulting artifacts propagate peer-to-peer without telemetry footprints.

conflicts.point: Whether compliance overhead from regulatory reporting thresholds protects public safety or functions as regulatory capture that harms open-source developers.

positions.stance: Prioritizes civilizational risk mitigation and systemic containment over open-source market access.
Prioritizes open-source developer access and market competition, arguing that regulatory burdens entrench corporate incumbents.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-training compute telemetry and export controls can effectively prevent the proliferation of frontier model capabilities.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position correctly distinguishes between low-compute cryptography like PGP and high-compute frontier models that require billion-dollar clusters. Semiconductor supply chains and massive energy requirements create tangible, physical chokepoints that regulators can monitor.

verdicts.conflict: Whether compliance overhead from regulatory reporting thresholds protects public safety or functions as regulatory capture that harms open-source developers.
verdicts.rationale: Critics provide concrete evidence that complex audit trails impose recurring financial costs that disproportionately burden independent developers compared to cloud giants. This creates a clear economic barrier to entry in the open-source ecosystem.
